partial_case.facts: The resident lives with her child in the ground floor flat of a converted 1-story house. The landlord has vulnerabilities recorded for the resident. In her formal complaint, the resident said there was an ongoing mouse infestation within her flat which the landlord had persistently failed to resolve. The resident said she wanted the landlord to address this issue. She later asked to be re-housed by the landlord after repeated attempts to resolve the issue were unsuccessful. The landlord raised a job with is pest contactor in relation to the resident's report of a mice infestation in the kitchen, bathroom, and bedrooms on 18 June 2024. The landlord raised a further job with is pest contactor in relation to another report of a mice infestation in the resident's kitchen, bathroom, and bedrooms on 18 November 2024. The resident raised a formal complaint about the landlord's handling of the mice infestation on 23 January 2025. She said mice had returned despite the visits from the landlord's pest control. This issue had reoccurred since 2009. She wanted the pest issue to be permanently resolved.
partial_case.ground_truth_outcome: Service failure found in both the landlord's handling of the resident's reports of an ongoing mice infestation and handling of the related complaint. Orders made for apology, compensation of £350 (including £190 previously offered), and review of failings.

There was a lengthy and unreasonable delay in providing its final complaint response despite repeated requests from the resident.

partial_case.statutory_basis: The Ombudsman's Complaint Handling Code (the Code) 1 April 2024 required landlords to acknowledge a complaint within 5 days and respond to stage 1 and 2 complaints within 10 and 20 working days, respectively.

partial_case.facts: The resident lives with her child in a ground-floor flat of a converted one-storey house, and the landlord had vulnerabilities recorded for her. She complained of an ongoing mouse infestation which she said the landlord had persistently failed to resolve, wanted the issue addressed, and later asked to be rehoused. The complaint concerned the landlord’s handling of reports of an ongoing mice infestation and the related complaint. The landlord raised pest-contractor jobs in June and November 2024. On 23 January 2025 the resident made a formal complaint, saying mice had returned despite pest-control visits, the issue had recurred since 2009, and she wanted a permanent resolution. She later escalated the complaint, repeated requests to escalate it, and asked to be urgently rehoused due to the ongoing pest issue. The landlord’s final complaint response stated that additional entry points had been identified and offered £190 compensation.
partial_case.ground_truth_outcome: Service failure was found in the landlord’s handling of both the ongoing mice infestation reports and the related complaint. The landlord was ordered to apologise, pay the resident £350 compensation including the £190 offered during the complaints process, and review the failings identified.

Its failure to follow pest control recommendations or monitor the situation, was inappropriate.
The failure to get structural repairs right at earliest opportunity led to multiple pest control visits which alone, did not adequately address the issue.
This amounts to an overall finding of service failure.
